items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1958-08-29
items.q: In fact I met him in San Diego about five months ago.

ctx.x: could do. You were playing with a different key than the rest of the band. That's right, with the rest of the band. You could raise up the pitch.

You could raise up the band. You could raise up the band. So I quit working on Bourbon Street and I went back to town and hanging around a while. And Sidney Desvind, who had one of the best bands in New Orleans, their piano player wanted to go on a vacation. Who was it, remember? William Huston, who was also the president of the music union then. And they had a lot of good piano players around there that was much better than me, such as Kato.
